plan: Hold patient session state in a single public `session` dict with exactly the four contract keys, cloned from a frozen initial template so begin/abandon reset deterministically.
Copy `appointments` in the constructor into an ordered list of {id, label} dicts and build an id set for O(1) validation of choices and corrections.

Implement `handle` as a dispatch table from action `type` to a handler; each handler validates everything first and mutates `session` only after all checks pass, guaranteeing invalid actions cannot corrupt accepted data.

Build every screen through one `_screen(prompt, messages)` helper that returns a fresh dict and attaches copied appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment`, otherwise an empty list.
Route all rejections through `_error(reason)`, which prefixes `Error:` to the first message and renders the prompt derived from the untouched current state, so errors never raise and never mutate.

Compute the next unmet prompt (`Confirm contact` -> `Choose appointment` -> `Review and complete`) from session state for accepted confirmations and corrections; use the fixed prompts for choice, completion, and abandonment per the contract.

Accept `action_source`/`screen_sink` as constructor-injected ports; `run_once` raises RuntimeError before calling either if one is missing, then reads one action, handles it, displays the screen exactly once, and returns the same screen object — making both ports trivially replaceable by unittest fakes.
mechanisms: authoritative session dictionary with mutate-only-after-validation handlers
pure screen-builder helper emitting fresh prompt/messages/choices dicts
dispatch table mapping action type to validating handler
single error-screen helper that prefixes Error: and leaves state untouched
constructor-copied appointment list plus id set for choice validation
constructor-injected action_source/screen_sink ports verified in run_once before use
